changes: p1: name changed to the standard regnal stem 'Jitāmitramalladeva'. 'sumati jaya' is part of the royal style, so it moves to titles. Roles king + commissioner kept: 'thva pustaka dayakā' means 'had this book made'.

p2 Bhāgīrāma: the vague role 'other' is removed and only 'minister' is kept. 'paramāna' is read as pramāṇa/pradhāna, an office title. He is not the scribe, so the catalogue's 'Scribe' field is wrong. Confidence raised to high because the Newari is clear.
Date: ce_approx changed from 1690 to 1689. NS 810 began in Kārtika 1689, so Kārtika śukla 9 of NS 810 falls in Oct/Nov 1689.

Notes: confirmed that Śaka 1553 and VS 1688 agree (both 1631 CE) and that jīvavāsara means Thursday. 'Śālihotra' is noted as a text title, not a person. Added that the place is not stated but Bhaktapur is implied by the king.
Purpose filled in: commissioned by the king.

relations.evidence: jayajitāmitramalladevasana thva pustaka dayakā, bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa

notes: The colophon has two dates. (1) An inherited date, probably from the exemplar: śāke 1553 tathā saṃvat 1688, Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 11, jīvavāsara (Thursday). Śaka 1553 + 78 = 1631 and VS 1688 − 57 = 1631, so the two eras agree (July/Aug 1631 CE). (2) The date of this copy: NS 810 Kārtika śukla 9, about Oct/Nov 1689 CE. That falls within Jitāmitra Malla's reign at Bhaktapur (1673–1696). 'śālihotrasya pustakaṃ' names the text tradition (Śālihotra, the hippiatric author), not a person connected with this copy. The catalogue lists Bhāgīrāma as scribe, but 'bhāgirāma paramānayāvelasa' only dates the copy to 'the time when Bhāgīrāma was pramāṇa/pradhāna (minister)'. Bhāgīrāma is known as a pradhāna of Bhaktapur under Jitāmitra Malla. The scribe is not named. The place of copying is not stated, though Bhaktapur is likely from the king.
